citation: Malek N, Mrowczynska E, Michrowska A, Mazurkiewicz E, Pavlyk I, Mazur AJ. Knockout of ACTB and ACTG1 with CRISPR/Cas9(D10A) Technique Shows that Non-Muscle beta and gamma Actin Are Not Equal in Relation to Human Melanoma Cells' Motility and Focal Adhesion Formation. Int J Mol Sci. 2020;21(8):2746.
description: ACTB and ACTG1 CRISPR knockouts in human cells were compensated by increased expression of the other cytoplasmic actin isoform and altered focal-adhesion biology. This directly connects loss of a cytoplasmic actin to an actin-remodeling response, but in a non-neuronal human cell line.

citation: Czermak P, Amman F, Jantsch MF, Cimatti L. Organ-wide profiling in mouse reveals high editing levels of Filamin B mRNA in the musculoskeletal system. RNA Biol. 2018;15(7):877-885.
description: This study profiled Filamin B RNA editing in mouse tissues and identified ADAR2, encoded by Adarb1, as the enzyme responsible for FLNB editing. It provides a target-specific ADARB1-to-FLNB bridge while leaving the effect on Flnb mRNA abundance unresolved.

citation: Altaf F, Vesely C, Sheikh AM, Munir R, Shah STA, Tariq A. Modulation of ADAR mRNA expression in patients with congenital heart defects. PLoS One. 2019;14(4):e0200968.
description: Adar2-null mouse hearts had strongly reduced FLNB RNA editing but did not show a detectable change in FLNB expression. This supports ADARB1 as an FLNB-modifying enzyme and shows why reduced Flnb abundance is not directly predicted.

citation: Xiong R, Siegel D, Ross D. The activation sequence of cellular protein handling systems after proteasomal inhibition in dopaminergic cells. Chem Biol Interact. 2013;204(2):116-124.
description: MG132 inhibition of proteasomes in a dopaminergic neuronal cell line activated the unfolded-protein response, autophagic flux, and heat-shock response. It is pharmacologic and complex-level support for stress signatures after loss of proteasome activity.

citation: Gavilan MP, Pintado C, Gavilan E, Jimenez S, Rios RM, Vitorica J, Castano A, Ruano D. Dysfunction of the unfolded protein response increases neurodegeneration in aged rat hippocampus following proteasome inhibition. Aging Cell. 2009;8(6):654-665.
description: Hippocampal proteasome inhibition in rats increased ubiquitinated proteins and engaged PERK, IRE1alpha, and ATF6alpha unfolded-protein-response arms in young animals. It supports the expectation that proteasome impairment can drive neuronal UPR/stress programs, with species, age, and modality differences.

citation: Feliciano DM, Lin TV, Hartman NW, Bartley CM, Kubera C, Hsieh L, Lafourcade C, O'Keefe RA, Bordey A. A circuitry and biochemical basis for tuberous sclerosis symptoms: from epilepsy to neurocognitive deficits. Int J Dev Neurosci. 2013;31(7):667-678.
description: The review summarizes evidence that TSC1 or TSC2 inactivation increases neuronal mTOR signaling and perturbs neuronal growth and circuit function. It gives a target-specific TSC-to-mTOR bridge but not a one-gene prediction for every snRNA-seq hit.

citation: Yuskaitis CJ, Rossitto LA, Gurnani S, Bainbridge E, Poduri A, Sahin M. Chronic mTORC1 inhibition rescues behavioral and biochemical deficits resulting from neuronal Depdc5 loss in mice. Hum Mol Genet. 2019;28(17):2952-2964.
description: Neuron-specific Depdc5 knockout caused neuronal mTORC1 hyperactivation measured by phospho-S6, and rapamycin rescued downstream mTORC1 signaling. This directly supports DEPDC5 as a negative regulator of neuronal mTORC1, while most transcript directions remain indirect.

citation: Peterson TR, Sengupta SS, Harris TE, Carmack AE, Kang SA, Balderas E, Guertin DA, Madden KL, Carpenter AE, Finck BN, Sabatini DM. mTOR complex 1 regulates lipin 1 localization to control the SREBP pathway. Cell. 2011;146(3):408-420.
description: mTORC1 promoted SREBP target-gene expression and lipid biosynthetic signaling through lipin 1. It provides a mechanistic bridge from mTORC1 activation to lipid/SREBP genes, but it was established outside neurons.

citation: Tariq K, Cullen E, Getz SA, Conching AKS, Goyette AR, Prina ML, Wang W, Li M, Weston MC, Luikart BW. Disruption of mTORC1 rescues neuronal overgrowth and synapse function dysregulated by Pten loss. Cell Rep. 2022;41(4):111574.
description: Pten loss in dentate gyrus granule neurons increased mTORC1-dependent neuronal growth and excitatory synaptic transmission, and rapamycin or Raptor knockout rescued those phenotypes. It supports PTEN loss as an mTORC1-activating neuronal perturbation but not the exact sparse transcriptional outputs.

citation: Arif W, Mathur B, Saikali MF, Chembazhi UV, Toohill K, Song YJ, Hao Q, Karimi S, Blue SM, Yee BA, Van Nostrand EL, Bangru S, Guzman G, Yeo GW, Prasanth KV, Anakk S, Cummins CL, Kalsotra A. Splicing factor SRSF1 deficiency in the liver triggers NASH-like pathology and cell death. Nat Commun. 2023;14:946.
description: Acute SRSF1 depletion caused widespread transcriptomic and proteomic disruption through RNA-DNA hybrids, DNA damage, and global inhibition of mRNA transcription and protein synthesis. The bridge is target-specific but hepatic, and it does not determine the signs of individual neuronal RNA-processing hits.

citation: Pervouchine D, Popov Y, Berry A, Borsari B, Frankish A, Guigo R. Integrative transcriptomic analysis suggests new autoregulatory splicing events coupled with nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Nucleic Acids Res. 2019;47(10):5293-5306.
description: Integrated eCLIP, RBP knockdown RNA-seq, and NMD inactivation nominated autoregulatory NMD-coupled splicing events for U2AF2 and other RNA-binding proteins. It supports an RNA-processing bridge for U2AF2 loss but does not directly predict the observed cell-type gene directions.
